examples.en: The constitution guarantees the right to equality of all citizens.

examples.ko: 그 규정은 평등권에 어긋난다는 의견이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say that rule goes against the right to equality.

examples.ko: 평등권은 사람이면 누구나 가지는 기본적인 권리예요.
examples.en: The right to equality is a basic right that every person has.

examples.ko: 장애인의 평등권을 지키기 위한 법이 만들어졌어요.
examples.en: A law was made to protect the equal rights of people with disabilities.
Equal rights issues often appear in the news.

examples.ko: 이 단체는 이주민의 평등권을 위해 활동해요.
examples.en: This group works for the equal rights of immigrants.

explain: '평등'은 일반적인 말이고, '평등권'은 법에서 보장하는 권리라는 느낌이에요. 보통 '평등권을 보장하다/침해하다/지키다'처럼 써요. 뉴스, 법, 사회 수업에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 법은 여성의 평등권을 침해한다는 비판을 받았어요.
phrases.en: That law was criticized for violating women's right to equality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리가 지켜지지 않았다고 말하는 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news and legal talk when a right has been violated.
phrases.en_equiv: to violate the right to equality

phrases.example: 모두의 평등권을 지키기 위해 법을 고쳤어요.
phrases.en: They revised the law to protect everyone's right to equality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리를 보호한다는 긍정적인 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the positive sense of protecting a right.
phrases.en_equiv: to protect the right to equality

phrases.en: Guaranteeing equal rights is the foundation of a democratic society.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사형으로 제목이나 글에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This noun form often appears in headlines and writing.

explain_en: '평등' (equality) is the general word, while '평등권' feels like a legally guaranteed right. It is usually used as '평등권을 보장하다/침해하다/지키다'. It appears often in news, law and social studies classes.

examples.en: An angry customer assaulted an employee.
People nearby stopped the person who was about to attack someone.
If you assault someone, you are punished by law.

examples.ko: 친구를 폭행한 학생이 학교에서 징계를 받았어요.
examples.en: The student who assaulted a friend was disciplined by the school.

examples.ko: 아이를 폭행하는 일은 절대 있어서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: Hitting a child must never happen.
He assaulted a coworker and lost his job.

explain: '폭행하다'는 사람을 때리거나 힘으로 해치는 행동에 써요. 뉴스와 법 이야기에서 자주 나오는 딱딱한 말이라 일상 대화에서는 '때리다'가 더 자연스러워요. '폭행을 당하다'처럼 피해를 말할 때도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: He was assaulted on the road at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피해를 입은 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the victim's point of view.

phrases.example: 어제 우리 동네에서 폭행 사건이 있었어요.
phrases.en: There was an assault case in our neighborhood yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase often used in the news.

phrases.en: You must not hit your friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '폭행하다'보다 이 말을 훨씬 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation this is used much more often than 'to assault'.

explain_en: 폭행하다 is used for hitting or harming a person by force. It's a stiff word common in news and legal talk, so in everyday conversation 때리다 sounds more natural. For the victim's side, people often say 폭행을 당하다.

examples.en: Abusing a child is punished by law.
A person who abused animals appeared on the news.
If a parent abuses a child, you have to report it.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 직원을 학대한다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that the company mistreats its employees.

examples.ko: 누구도 약한 사람을 학대해서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: No one should mistreat a weaker person.
I saw a video of someone abusing a cat and reported it.

explain: 힘이 약한 사람이나 동물에게 몸과 마음의 상처를 주는 심각한 일에 써요. 가볍게 놀리는 정도에는 안 써요. 당한 쪽은 '학대를 당하다', '학대받다'라고 해요. '괴롭히다'보다 훨씬 무겁고 법과 뉴스에 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: That child was abused for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학대받은 쪽에서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person who suffered the abuse.

phrases.en: You must not abuse animals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약한 동물에게 해를 주는 일을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for harming weak animals.

phrases.en: Child abuse must be reported.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스와 법에서 자주 나오는 명사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase common in news and law.

explain_en: Cruel treatment of people or animals (동물 학대), strongly negative. It refers to serious harm done to the body or mind of someone weaker, such as a child or an animal, and is not used for light teasing. The victim is described as 학대를 당하다 or 학대받다. It is much heavier than 괴롭히다 (to bother, bully) and often appears in law and the news.

t90.ax: Abusing a child is punished by law.

en: to be liberated; to be set free; to be emancipated

examples.en: The exam is over, so I'm free from studying.
When I leave work, I feel freed from it.
I'm free from a long worry, so I feel at ease.
Korea was liberated from Japan in 1945.

examples.ko: 집안일에서 해방될 수 있는 방법이 없을까요?
examples.en: Isn't there a way to get free from housework?
The liberated people came out to the streets and rejoiced.

explain: 일상에서는 '벗어나다', '자유로워지다'를 쓰고, '해방되다'는 힘들던 일이나 억압에서 벗어난 기쁨을 크게 말할 때 써요. 역사 이야기에서는 1945년 광복을 '해방'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I finally got free from the hard work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more everyday word.

phrases.en: It's vacation, so my body and mind feel free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얽매인 것이 없어져 편안해진 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the relaxed state of no longer being tied down.

phrases.en: With the exams over, I feel a sense of liberation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해방'에 '감'을 붙여 그 기분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 감 to 해방 names that feeling.

explain_en: In daily life '벗어나다' or '자유로워지다' fit; '해방되다' stresses the joy of escaping something hard or oppressive. In history, the 1945 liberation is also called '해방'.

en: to donate; to contribute; to give offerings

examples.en: Church members donated for the church's construction.
I give part of my salary as an offering every month.
I haven't decided yet how much to give.
Many people give offerings out of gratitude.
After giving the offering, I felt at ease.
They set up a scholarship with the money my friend donated.

explain: '기부하다'와 비슷하지만 종교 단체에 돈을 낼 때 주로 써요. 일반 단체나 학교에 돈을 낼 때는 '기부하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I went to church for the first time and gave an offering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '헌금하다'를 명사로 풀어 쓴 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form that spells out 헌금하다 with the noun.

phrases.en: I want to donate for the new building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이나 마음을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to express a wish or intention.

phrases.en: I donated books to the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종교 단체가 아닌 곳에 돈이나 물건을 줄 때는 이 말이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural when giving money or goods to places that aren't religious groups.

explain_en: Giving money at church or temple (교회에서 헌금하다) It is similar to '기부하다', but it is mainly used for giving money to a religious organization. For ordinary organizations or schools, '기부하다' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: I haven't decided yet how much to give.

examples.ko: 이 행동은 형법에 따라 처벌받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: This act can be punished under the criminal law.
I have a friend who studies criminal law at university.

examples.ko: 형법은 어떤 행동이 범죄인지 정해 놓은 법이에요.
examples.en: Criminal law is the law that sets which acts count as crimes.
The revised criminal law takes effect next month.
Please explain the difference between criminal law and civil law.

examples.ko: 변호사 시험에 형법 문제가 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many criminal law questions came up on the bar exam.

explain: 형법은 범죄와 벌을 다루고, 민법은 사람 사이의 재산·가족 문제를 다뤄요. 그래서 도둑질이나 폭행은 형법 이야기고, 계약이나 이혼은 민법 이야기예요. 법 이름이라 '형법 제○조'처럼 숫자와 함께 자주 써요.

phrases.en: If you break the criminal law, you can be punished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법을 지키지 않았다는 뜻으로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing meaning not obeying the law.

phrases.en: This kind of behavior is a crime under criminal law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형법의 기준으로 볼 때라는 뜻으로 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that something is so by the standard of criminal law.

phrases.en: Article 250 of the Criminal Act is the provision on murder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법 조문을 말할 때 숫자와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a number when citing a statute.

explain_en: The criminal law deals with crimes and punishment, while the civil law deals with property and family matters between people. So theft and assault are criminal law, while contracts and divorce are civil law. As a law's name it often appears with numbers, as in '형법 제○조'.

examples.en: An employee embezzled company money.

examples.ko: 그는 모임 회비를 횡령해서 모두를 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: He embezzled the club dues and shocked everyone.

examples.ko: 돈을 횡령하면 법에 따라 벌을 받아요.
examples.en: If you embezzle money, you are punished by law.
The person who tried to embezzle money was found out early.

examples.ko: 경리가 몰래 횡령하고 있었다는 사실이 밝혀졌어요.
examples.en: It came out that the accountant had been secretly embezzling.

examples.ko: 공금을 횡령할 생각은 절대 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must never think of embezzling public funds.

explain: '공금을 횡령하다', '돈을 횡령하다'처럼 목적어에 돈이나 물건이 와요. 맡은 것을 쓰는 거라서 '훔치다'와 다르고, 뉴스에서는 '횡령 혐의'로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That employee embezzled public funds and was fired.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적어로 돈이 올 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with money as the object.

phrases.en: He returned all the money he had embezzled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여서 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-ㄴ' lets the verb describe the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 남이 맡긴 돈을 횡령하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not embezzle money that someone else entrusted to you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 도덕을 말할 때 쓰는 금지 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A prohibition form used for rules or morals.

explain_en: The object is money or goods, as in '공금을 횡령하다' (embezzle public funds). Because the money was entrusted to you, it differs from '훔치다' (steal), and in the news it often appears as '횡령 혐의' (suspicion of embezzlement).

en: to damage; to harm; to deface

examples.en: Someone damaged the trees in the park.
If you damage a cultural property, you must pay a fine.
A false rumor damaged his reputation.
I oppose development that damages nature.
I damaged a library book and had to pay for it.
We must be careful not to damage trust.

explain: '망가뜨리다'보다 딱딱하고, 문화재, 자연, 명예, 신뢰처럼 소중한 것을 상하게 할 때 써요. 컵이나 장난감이 부서지는 일에는 어울리지 않아요. 뉴스와 법 이야기에서 '명예 훼손', '문화재 훼손'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The old painting was damaged by the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소중한 것이 상한 결과를 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, stating that something valuable has been damaged.

phrases.example: 거짓말로 남의 명예를 훼손하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not harm someone's reputation with lies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 좋은 평판을 해친다는 뜻으로 뉴스와 법에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means harming a person's good reputation and is common in news and law.

phrases.en: Please don't damage the mural in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 소중한 것을 상하게 하지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices to ask people not to damage something valuable.

explain_en: Someone defaces or tarnishes; formal, honor, property, cultural assets. Stiffer than 망가뜨리다 (break, ruin), it is used for harming valuable things such as cultural property, nature, reputation or trust. It doesn't suit a broken cup or toy. In the news you will see 명예 훼손 (defamation) and 문화재 훼손 (damage to cultural property).

t90.ax: A false rumor damaged his reputation.

examples.en: The fact that time flows is an unchanging truth.
In this experiment, the temperature is always constant.

examples.ko: 세상에 불변이란 없다는 말을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: I often hear the saying that nothing in the world is unchanging.

examples.ko: 계약 기간 동안 가격은 불변으로 유지돼요.
examples.en: The price is kept fixed during the contract period.
Some people believe that love never changes.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 수십 년 동안 불변인 맛으로 사랑받았어요.
examples.en: That shop has been loved for decades for its unchanging taste.

explain: 변하지 않는다는 뜻으로, 보통 '불변의 진리/법칙/원칙'처럼 '불변의' 모양으로 써요. 반대말은 '가변'이나 '변화'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '변하지 않다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 모든 사람은 언젠가 죽는다는 것이 불변의 진리예요.
phrases.en: It is an unchanging truth that everyone dies someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불변'이 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the pairing in which 불변 appears most often.

phrases.example: 물은 높은 곳에서 낮은 곳으로 흐른다는 것은 불변의 법칙이에요.
phrases.en: Water flowing from high to low is an unchanging law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학이나 자연의 규칙을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is often used for scientific or natural rules.

phrases.example: 우리 사이는 앞으로도 변하지 않을 거예요.
phrases.en: Our relationship will not change in the future either.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '불변'보다 이 말이 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation this sounds much more natural than 불변.

explain_en: It means not changing, and is usually used in the form '불변의', as in '불변의 진리', '불변의 법칙' and '불변의 원칙'. Its opposites are '가변' and '변화'. In everyday talk, '변하지 않다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 마당의 소나무는 사철 푸르러서 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: The pine tree in the yard stays green all year, which looks nice.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 사철 손님이 끊이지 않아요.
examples.en: This restaurant has customers all year round.
Jeju Island has many tourists all year round.

examples.ko: 사철 입을 수 있는 얇은 재킷을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a thin jacket I can wear in every season.

examples.ko: 이 꽃은 사철 피어서 정원에 심었어요.
examples.en: This flower blooms all year, so I planted it in the garden.
Evergreen trees look pretty even in winter.

explain: '사계절'과 같은 뜻이지만 '사철 푸른 나무', '사철 내내'처럼 일 년 내내라는 뜻으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 주로 부사처럼 뒤에 서술어가 바로 와요. '농사철', '이사철'처럼 '-철'은 어떤 일이 많은 때를 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 지역은 사철 내내 관광객이 많아요.
phrases.en: This area has many tourists all year round.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일 년 내내라는 뜻을 더 강하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes the meaning of 'throughout the entire year'.

phrases.en: Korea has four distinct seasons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 봄, 여름, 가을, 겨울 네 계절 자체를 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but more natural when referring to the four seasons themselves.

phrases.en: Flowers bloom all year in the greenhouse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일 년 내내 계속되는 일을 말할 때 부사처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like an adverb for something that continues all year.

explain_en: Through every season, used adverbially (사철 내내) It matches '사계절', but is often used to mean 'all year round', as in '사철 푸른 나무' or '사철 내내'. It mostly works like an adverb, followed directly by the predicate. The suffix '-철' in words like '농사철' and '이사철' marks a busy season for something.

examples.ko: 생로병사는 누구도 피할 수 없는 일이에요.
examples.en: Birth, aging, sickness and death are something no one can avoid.
My grandmother says that birth, aging, sickness and death are natural.

examples.ko: 이 다큐는 사람의 생로병사를 따라가며 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This documentary follows and shows the whole course of human life.

examples.ko: 부처님은 생로병사의 고통에서 벗어나는 길을 찾았다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the Buddha found a way out of the suffering of birth, aging, sickness and death.

examples.ko: 오늘은 생로병사에 대해 깊이 생각하게 된 하루였어요.
examples.en: Today was a day when I thought deeply about life and death.

examples.ko: 생로병사 같은 큰 주제는 윤리 시간에도 배워요.
examples.en: Big topics like birth, aging, sickness and death are also taught in ethics class.

explain: 원래는 불교에서 나온 말이지만, 지금은 사람이 태어나서 늙고 병들고 죽는 인생 전체를 말할 때 두루 써요. '생로병사의 과정', '생로병사의 비밀'처럼 '의'와 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The process of birth, aging, sickness, and death comes to everyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'와 함께 써서 인생 전체의 흐름을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '의', it describes the whole flow of a life.

phrases.example: 과학자들은 생로병사의 비밀을 알고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: Scientists want to learn the secrets of birth, aging, sickness, and death.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책이나 방송 제목에서 자주 보는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in book and TV program titles.
phrases.en_equiv: the secrets of birth, aging, sickness, and death

phrases.example: 병원에서 일하면 생로병사를 가까이에서 지켜보게 돼요.
phrases.en: Working in a hospital, you get to watch birth, aging, sickness, and death up close.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의' 없이 목적어로 써서 인생의 여러 순간을 직접 본다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as an object without '의', meaning one sees life's stages firsthand.
phrases.en_equiv: to witness the stages of life

explain_en: It comes from Buddhism, but now it is widely used for the whole course of human life: being born, growing old, falling sick and dying. It often appears with '의', as in '생로병사의 과정'.

en: belief that domestic farm products are the best

examples.ko: 신토불이라고 우리 땅에서 난 쌀이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: They say local is best, and rice grown in our own land tastes the best.

examples.ko: 시장에 신토불이 농산물 코너가 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new corner for locally grown produce opened at the market.
My grandmother always stresses eating local produce.
Since local is best, I always buy domestic kimchi.

examples.ko: 요즘은 신토불이보다 가격을 먼저 보는 사람도 많아요.
examples.en: These days many people look at the price before the 'buy local' idea.

examples.ko: 신토불이에 관심이 많아서 지역 장터를 자주 가요.
examples.en: I'm interested in eating local, so I often go to the regional market.

explain: 주로 국산 농산물이나 음식을 홍보하는 간판과 광고 문구에서 많이 보여요. 단순히 '국산'이라고 하는 것보다 우리 땅에서 난 것을 아끼는 마음이 담겨 있어요.

phrases.en: Food grown in our own land is good for the body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우리 땅에서 난 재료로 만든 음식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for food made from ingredients grown in our own land.

phrases.en: A market for homegrown foods has opened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장터나 행사 이름에 자주 붙는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in the names of markets and events.

phrases.example: 우리 땅에서 난 채소로 만든 반찬이에요.
phrases.en: This side dish is made with vegetables grown in our land.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신토불이'의 뜻을 쉽게 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to spell out the meaning of 신토불이.

explain_en: You mostly see it on signs and in ads promoting domestic produce and food. Rather than just saying '국산' (domestic), it carries the feeling of valuing what grows on our own land.

en: to be valuable; to be precious; to be noble

examples.en: Every human being is a precious existence.
Life is precious to everyone.

examples.ko: 신분이 존귀하다고 해서 남을 무시하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even if your status is high, you must not look down on others.
Everyone has the right to be treated with dignity.
There is no life that is not precious.

examples.ko: 아이들에게 모든 생명이 존귀하다는 것을 가르쳐요.
examples.en: I teach children that all life is precious.

explain: 딱딱한 한자어라서 글이나 연설에서 주로 써요. 일상에서는 '귀하다'(귀한 손님)나 '소중하다'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 존귀한 생명을 함부로 해치면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not harm precious life carelessly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생명이나 인간의 가치를 높여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to speak highly of the value of life or humans.

phrases.en: Everyone is precious.
phrases.nuance_ko: '존귀하다'의 해요체로, 말할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The haeyo form, usable in speech.

phrases.en: My family is the most precious to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '존귀하다'보다 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used much more often than '존귀하다' in daily speech.

explain_en: Formal; high inherent dignity, such as human life or a person. This is a stiff Sino-Korean word used mostly in writing and speeches. In everyday talk people more often say '귀하다' (as in 귀한 손님) or '소중하다'.

examples.en: At church we praise God with songs.
People praised that hero's courage.

examples.ko: 봄을 찬양하는 시를 한 편 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a poem that celebrates spring.
When I sing praise loudly, my heart feels at ease.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 사랑을 찬양한 노래로 유명해요.
examples.en: That singer is famous for a song praising love.

examples.ko: 무조건 찬양하기만 하면 문제를 못 봐요.
examples.en: If you only keep praising something, you cannot see its problems.

explain: '찬양하다'는 크게 높여서 칭찬한다는 느낌이라서 종교나 시, 노래에 많이 나와요. 보통 칭찬은 '칭찬하다'를 쓰고, 일상에서 '찬양하다'를 쓰면 너무 과장돼요. 교회에서는 노래로 하나님을 높이는 시간을 '찬양'이라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 교회에서 찬양 시간에 다 같이 노래해요.
phrases.en: At church, everyone sings together during praise time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '찬양하다'의 명사형으로, 노래로 높이는 시간을 말하기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form; it can also mean a time of singing praise.

phrases.en: The poet wrote a poem praising nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 와서 '높이 칭찬하는 ~'이라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it means '~ that praises'.

phrases.example: 그 의사는 많은 사람들에게 찬양을 받았어요.
phrases.en: That doctor was praised by many people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 칭찬받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the one being greatly praised.

explain_en: Lofty, almost reverent praise, also religious worship songs. 찬양하다 means praising someone very highly, so it appears in religion, poetry and songs. For ordinary praise you use 칭찬하다, and 찬양하다 in daily talk sounds exaggerated. In church, the singing time to honor God is called 찬양.

t90.ax: At church we praise God with songs.
